literal: seeking the worthy and examining officeholders—reason demands careful scrutiny.
idiomatic: seeking the worthy and examining officeholders demands careful scrutiny.

literal: Now Shenhuan came from dyeing work with nothing extraordinary; he merely used family wealth to gain access and now stands among Jin gentry—a thing that truly fears the pelican's sting reaching foreign borders.
idiomatic: Now Shenhuan came from dyeing with nothing extraordinary; he merely bought his way among Jin gentry—a thing that truly fears the pelican's sting will reach foreign borders.

literal: Hu in the end shelved the matter.
idiomatic: Hu in the end shelved the matter.

literal: He was transferred to Junior Inner History Grandee.
idiomatic: He was transferred to junior inner history grandee.

literal: Emperor Wu was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to select old oxen to feast the troops.
idiomatic: Wu Di was at Yunyang Palace and ordered the garrisons to pick old oxen to feast the troops.

literal: Kai remonstrated: "Formerly Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—the gentleman took it as a fine tale.
idiomatic: Kai remonstrated: "Formerly Tian Zifang ransomed an old horse—the gentleman praised it."

literal: Now following the bright edict to feast the troops with old oxen harms humane government.
idiomatic: Now following the edict to feast the troops with old oxen harms humane government.

literal: The Emperor praised his words and stopped.
idiomatic: The emperor praised his words and stopped.

literal: He was transferred to Grandee of the Ministry of Rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grandee of the ministry of rites and served as deputy on the embassy to Chen.

literal: Earlier envoys mostly followed Chen ritual; when Kai was envoy he followed his own court entirely, and Chen men could not bend him.
idiomatic: Earlier envoys mostly followed Chen ritual; when Kai was envoy he followed his own court entirely, and the Chen could not bend him.

literal: In the fourth year of Jiande Li Mu captured the garrisons of Zhiguan and Baiya and ordered Kai to compose a victory bulletin.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiande Li Mu captured Zhiguan and Baiya garrisons and ordered Kai to compose a victory bulletin.

literal: The Emperor read it and greatly rejoiced: "Lu Kai's writing has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian is indeed Lord Ling's son."
idiomatic: The emperor read it and rejoiced: "Lu Kai's writing has greatly advanced—Xun Jingqian is indeed Lord Ling's son."

literal: In the first year of Daxiang he was appointed Grandee of the Eastern Capital Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he was grandee of the eastern capital ministry of personnel.

literal: At the beginning of Sui Kai Kai was given superior protocol equal to Three Excellencies and made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui he was given superior protocol equal to the Three Excellencies and made vice director of the ministry of personnel.

literal: He was advanced to Marquis and still held concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was advanced to marquis and still held concurrent left vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Whenever he memorialized he spoke forthrightly with proper color; even meeting anger or joy he did not change his constant manner.
idiomatic: Whenever he memorialized he spoke forthrightly; even meeting anger or joy he did not change.

literal: He was given addition as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: He was given addition as regular attendant.

literal: In the eighth year the Emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai first; he firmly declined and dared not accept.
idiomatic: In the eighth year the emperor personally examined the hundred officials and ranked Kai first; he firmly declined.

literal: Emperor Wen said: "When duty calls one does not yield—what shame is there?
idiomatic: Wen Di said: "When duty calls one does not yield—what shame is there?"

literal: All is in Our heart; no need for false modesty.
idiomatic: All is in my heart; no need for false modesty."

literal: After more than a year he was appointed Minister of Rites, holding charge of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: After more than a year he was minister of rites, holding charge of the ministry of personnel.

literal: When National University Erudite He Tuo and Right Vice Director Su Wei were at odds, Tuo memorialized Wei's secret matters and Kai sat connected.
idiomatic: When national university erudite He Tuo and right vice director Su Wei quarreled, Tuo memorialized Wei's secret matters and Kai was implicated.

literal: The censorate memorialized Kai: "Fang Gongyi was a partisan of Yu Chi Tong and ought not to advance in office.
idiomatic: The censorate memorialized Kai: "Fang Gongyi was Yu Chi Tong's partisan and ought not to advance."

literal: Wei and Kai bent the rules to recommend and advance him, repeatedly promoting him to Governor of Haizhou.
idiomatic: Wei and Kai bent the rules to recommend him, repeatedly promoting him to governor of Haizhou.

literal: Many were pre-selected in the Ministry of Personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked their names in color and sent them away.
idiomatic: Many were pre-selected in the ministry of personnel; Kai did not immediately grant office but marked their names in color and sent them away.

literal: Wei's younger cousins Che and Su were both summoned as village rectifiers to the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: Wei's younger cousins Che and Su were both summoned as village rectifiers to the ministry of personnel.

literal: Che's literary documents arrived late yet he was appointed first.
idiomatic: Che's documents arrived late yet he was appointed first.

literal: Su's left foot was crippled and his talent was unmeasured; Kai because of Wei made him Gentleman for Palace Attendance.
idiomatic: Su's left foot was crippled and his talent unmeasured; Kai because of Wei made him gentleman for palace attendance.

literal: Kai's factional conduct was very clear.
idiomatic: Kai's factional conduct was very clear.

literal: The Emperor was greatly angered: "Kai dares to treat the celestial offices as private favor!"
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered: "Kai dares to treat the celestial offices as private favor!"

literal: Kai doffed his cap and knocked his head: "The crown prince was about to make Su Kui of the Communications Office a palace attendant.
idiomatic: Kai doffed his cap and knocked his head: "The crown prince was about to make Su Kui of the communications office a palace attendant."

literal: Kui is Wei's son; your servant held Kui unfit for promotion and firmly remonstrated to stop it.
idiomatic: Kui is Wei's son; I held Kui unfit and firmly remonstrated to stop it.

literal: If I had private dealings with Wei, would I have acted thus?"
idiomatic: Had I private dealings with Wei, would I have done so?"

literal: The Emperor said: "Wei's son the court all knows; you were obstinate to seek personal fortune;
idiomatic: The emperor said: "Wei's son the court all knows; you were obstinate to seek fortune;"

literal: what you did not know you carried out as factional support.
idiomatic: what you did not know, you backed as faction.

literal: That is the conduct of a treacherous minister.
idiomatic: That is the conduct of a treacherous minister."

literal: Thereupon he was removed from name and died at home.
idiomatic: He was removed from office and died at home.

literal: From the Zhou house onward selection had no clear or muddy.
idiomatic: From Zhou onward office selection had neither clear nor muddy ranks.

literal: When Kai held charge of the Ministry of Personnel, with Xue Daoheng, Lu Yanshi, and others he sorted the gentry stream—hence he fell into the calumny of partisan prohibition and came to this.
idiomatic: When Kai held the ministry of personnel, with Xue Daoheng and Lu Yanshi he sorted the gentry stream—hence he fell into partisan calumny and came to this.

literal: Chong's younger brother Zhongyi, styled Xiaohei, was renowned in the world, post: Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant, Governor of Youzhou.
idiomatic: Chong's brother Zhongyi, styled Xiaohei, was renowned, reaching supernumerary regular cavalier attendant and governor of Youzhou.

literal: Chong's brothers' offices though not high, their marriages were always equal to Xuan's house.
idiomatic: Though Chong's brothers never rose high, their marriages always matched Xuan's house.

literal: Hong's younger brother Guangzong, post: Director in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Hong's brother Guangzong was director in the masters of writing.

literal: Guangzong's son was Guan.
idiomatic: Guangzong's son was Guan.

literal: Guan's younger brother Zhongxuan, childhood name Jin.
idiomatic: Guan's brother Zhongxuan, childhood name Jin.

literal: His learning was broad and harmonious and surpassed Guan, but his literary style was rather fine-grained.
idiomatic: His learning was broad and surpassed Guan, but his style was rather fine.

literal: The brothers were all famed for literature; opinion praised them.
idiomatic: The brothers all won fame in letters, and opinion praised them.

literal: Post: Aide in the Grand Marshal's office.
idiomatic: He reached aide in the grand marshal's office.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei he was killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang of Wei he was killed at Heyin.

literal: He and his elder brother Guan both had no sons; collected works were not compiled and few survive.
idiomatic: He and his brother Guan both had no sons; collected works were not compiled and few survive.

literal: Zhongxuan's younger brother Shubiao.
idiomatic: Zhongxuan's brother was Shubiao.

literal: Shubiao in his district had a thousand piculs of grain; each spring and summer when villagers had no food he let them load and take.
idiomatic: Shubiao kept a thousand piculs in his district; each spring and summer when neighbors had no food he let them load what they needed.

literal: In autumn he let them return the price without reckoning.
idiomatic: In autumn he let them repay the price without counting interest.

literal: Year after year he regularly gained more than double.
idiomatic: Year after year he still came out more than double ahead.

literal: Once in court at high rank, seeing himself old with many sons, he built a great house and said: "We sing here, we weep here."
idiomatic: Once he stood high in court, old and with many sons, he built a great house and said, "Here we sing; here we weep."

literal: Wei Shou often came to visit him and asked about old matters of the Luoyang capital.
idiomatic: Wei Shou often came to visit and asked about old Luoyang matters.

literal: Without waiting for food he would rise and say: "Hard to be a burden on the young."
idiomatic: Without waiting for food he would rise and say: "Hard to burden the young."

literal: Shubiao kept him; long after, food came—only millet meal and sunflower greens in a wooden bowl, with a slice of dried meat.
idiomatic: Shubiao kept him; long after food came—only millet meal and sunflower greens in a wooden bowl, with a slice of dried meat.

literal: The servants he brought were all fed the same.
idiomatic: The servants he brought were all fed the same.

literal: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang.
idiomatic: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang.

literal: In the chaos the city fell; he and his cousin Shi Sui both died of cold and hunger.
idiomatic: In the chaos the city fell; he and his cousin Shi Sui both perished of cold and hunger.

literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, because the two had fame and virtue, collected and buried them.
idiomatic: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, honoring their fame and virtue, gathered and buried them.

literal: Hong's younger cousin Fubo; Fubo's younger brother Shibo—both had learning.
idiomatic: Hong's cousin Fubo; Fubo's brother Shibo—both had learning.

literal: Fubo, post: Chief Clerk of Pingdong Office in Cangzhou; Shibo, Governor of Southern Qi.
idiomatic: Fubo was chief clerk of Pingdong office in Cangzhou; Shibo was governor of southern Qi.

literal: Shibo's younger cousin Wenwei.
idiomatic: Shibo's cousin was Wenwei.

literal: Wenwei, styled Xiuzu.
idiomatic: Wenwei was styled Xiuzu.

literal: His father Chang, post: Gentleman for Discussion, later because of Wenwei's merit enfeoffed Governor of Youzhou posthumously.
idiomatic: His father Chang was gentleman for discussion; later because of Wenwei's merit he was posthumously enfeoffed governor of Youzhou.

literal: Wenwei was orphaned young, had ambition, and ranged somewhat through classics and histories.
idiomatic: Wenwei lost his father young, had ambition, and read somewhat in the classics and histories.

literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk.
idiomatic: The province summoned him as chief clerk.

literal: At thirty-eight he first passed the cultivated-talent examination and was made Chief Clerk of the Long Flow in the Pacify-the-North Office of the province.
idiomatic: At thirty-eight he first passed the cultivated-talent examination and was made chief clerk of the long flow in the pacify-the-north office.

literal: He persuaded Governor Pei Jun to repair the Duguang embankment by old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing of fields; people relied on the benefit.
idiomatic: He persuaded Governor Pei Jun to repair the Duguang embankment by old traces, irrigating more than ten thousand qing; people relied on the benefit.

literal: Jun's merit in the repair he largely entrusted to him.
idiomatic: Jun largely entrusted the repair to him.

literal: Wenwei was skilled at management and also expended private effort; the family had always been poor and frugal, and thereby grew rich.
idiomatic: Wenwei was skilled at management and also spent private effort; the family had always been poor and frugal, and thereby grew rich.

literal: When the north was about to fall into chaos, Wenwei stored grain in Fanyang city; in years of famine he gave much relief and was all the more trusted by the district.
idiomatic: When the north was about to fall into chaos, Wenwei stored grain in Fanyang; in famine years he gave much relief and was all the more trusted by the district.

literal: When Han Lou held Jicheng, Wenwei led the district to defend Fanyang.
idiomatic: When Han Lou seized Jicheng, Wenwei led the district in defending Fanyang.

literal: When Lou was pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia and made Administrator of Fanyang.
idiomatic: When Lou was pacified, for merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Daxia and made administrator of Fanyang.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang of Wei died, Wenwei plotted uprising with Youzhou Governor Liu Lingzhu.
idiomatic: When Zhuang Di of Wei died, Wenwei plotted uprising with Youzhou governor Liu Lingzhu.

literal: Lingzhu took Yingzhou and left Wenwei to act for the province; he himself led troops to Dingzhou and was defeated by Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen.
idiomatic: Lingzhu took Yingzhou and left Wenwei to act for the province; he led troops to Dingzhou and was defeated by Erzhu Rong's general Hou Shen.

literal: Wenwei fled back to his commandery and still moved in concert with the Gao brothers.
idiomatic: Wenwei fled home and still acted in concert with the Gao brothers.

literal: When Shenwu reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with a memorial of apology.
idiomatic: When Shenwu reached Xindu, Wenwei sent his son Huaidao with an apology.

literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Governor of Anzhou but did not take office; soon transferred to Governor of Youzhou.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made governor of Anzhou but did not take office; soon transferred to governor of Youzhou.

literal: Anzhou Governor Lu Cao also followed Lingzhu in raising troops.
idiomatic: Anzhou governor Lu Cao also followed Lingzhu in raising troops.

literal: When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao then held Youzhou and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: When Lingzhu was defeated, Cao held Youzhou and surrendered to Erzhu Zhao.

literal: Zhao still made him governor; he held the city and would not descend, and Wenwei could not enter.
idiomatic: Zhao still made him governor; he held the city and would not yield, and Wenwei could not enter.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Qingzhou.

literal: Wenwei was light with wealth and loved guests, skilled at soothing;
idiomatic: Wenwei spent freely and loved guests, and was skilled at winning men;

literal: he liked to do small favors.
idiomatic: he liked to do small favors.

literal: Hence wherever he went he largely won people's hearts.
idiomatic: Wherever he went he largely won people's hearts.

literal: Managing livelihood he was always as if insufficient; amassing wealth and gathering stores, he attended on favor and power and gifts never ceased.
idiomatic: Managing livelihood he was always as if insufficient; amassing wealth, he attended on favor and power and gifts never ceased.

literal: He died; posthumously enfeoffed Duke of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, posthumous title Xiaowei.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously enfeoffed duke of the secretariat, right vice director of the masters of writing, posthumous title Xiaowei.

literal: His son Gongdao was gentle and kind and had some literary learning.
idiomatic: His son Gongdao was gentle, kind, and had some learning in letters.

literal: Post: Administrator of Fanyang Commandery, with virtue and grace.
idiomatic: He was administrator of Fanyang commandery, with virtue and grace.

literal: He died before Wenwei.
idiomatic: He died before Wenwei.

literal: Posthumously enfeoffed Director of Revenue, posthumous title Ding.
idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed director of revenue, posthumous title Ding.

literal: His son Xunzu inherited the grandfather's enfeoffment as Baron of Daxia.
idiomatic: His son Xunzu inherited his grandfather's barony of Daxia.

literal: He had technical learning and splendid literary style—a outstanding man of the later generation.
idiomatic: He had technical learning and splendid style—a outstanding man of his generation.

literal: He passed the cultivated-talent examination and reached Ye.
idiomatic: He passed the cultivated-talent examination and went to Ye.

literal: Zhao commandery Li Zuxun once feasted various literary gentlemen.
idiomatic: Li Zuxun of Zhao commandery once feasted various literary gentlemen.

literal: Qi Wensuan sent a minor yellow gate to instruct Zuxun's mother: "The Rouran are broken—why no congratulatory memorial?"
idiomatic: Wensuan sent a minor yellow gate to tell Zuxun's mother: "The Rouran are broken—where is your congratulatory memorial?"

literal: The envoy waited.
idiomatic: The envoy waited.

literal: All the guests composed memorials; Xunzu finished his in a moment.
idiomatic: All the guests wrote memorials; Xunzu finished his in an instant.
